Title: February 19, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting
Overview: The Boulder City Council held its regular Thursday meeting, opening with extensive public comment, mostly from residents urging the city to keep the lap pool at the South Boulder Rec Center. The council unanimously approved the consent agenda and adopted resolution 1370 and ordinance 8734 to annex about 24 acres of city-owned Hogan-Pancost land, along with a land use map change for future parks and flood mitigation. Council also gave non-binding feedback on a concept plan for 281 apartments at 4880 Pearl Street, with members concerned about eroding industrial land.

Topic1.Title: Open Comment and South Boulder Rec Center Pool
Topic1.Summary: Residents, students, and families spoke during open comment, with most urging council to preserve the lap pool, gym, and cardio at the South Boulder Rec Center. Speakers cited its walkability, its role for Fairview swim team and schools, and a city petition with thousands of signatures. Other speakers raised concerns about foreign policy, a dog program, and homelessness and ambulance care. Council thanked the speakers, and staff said no decisions had been made on the rec center, which received $2 million in the 2025 budget, with study sessions planned for March and April.

Topic2.Title: Staff Responses to Open Comment
Topic2.Summary: Staff responded to open comment on the city's new ambulance provider and an allegation of chemical sedation by the former provider, noting the related lawsuit was dismissed. Staff also said they would follow up on the Voice and Sight dog program concerns. Council members asked follow-up questions and thanked youth speakers and South Boulder residents.

Topic3.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic3.Summary: Council considered consent agenda item 3, which included items 3A and 3B. Council members asked no questions, and a motion and second were made. The consent agenda was approved unanimously by roll call.

Topic4.Title: Annexation and Land Use Change for Hogan-Pancost Property
Topic4.Summary: Council held a public hearing on annexing about 24 acres of city-owned Hogan-Pancost property and a portion of 55th Street right-of-way. Staff and Parks and Recreation described future flood mitigation and parks uses on the western portion, with open space preserved east of 55th Street. The annexation adopted resolution 1370 and ordinance 8734 with public zoning and RL2 zoning for the right-of-way, and the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan map change was approved. All votes were unanimous, and no public speakers were able to testify due to connection issues.

Topic5.Title: Concept Review for 4880 Pearl Street Residential Project
Topic5.Summary: Council reviewed a concept plan for redeveloping the Boulder Storage site with four residential buildings containing 281 apartments and an 85,000-square-foot storage building. Staff said the General Industrial land use and IG zoning likely make residential inconsistent with the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan and East Boulder subcommunity plan, and raised contiguity and phasing concerns. Council members expressed concern about losing industrial land, the precedent for nearby parcels, and the need for more clarity on contiguity rules. No formal action was taken, and the applicant was asked to return with a revised concept.
